newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Peat Board year net profit 4.8 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Irish Peat Board year net profit 4.8 mln punts.

text.p: The Irish Peat Board, Bord na Mona, said on Wednesday that it made a net profit of 4.8 million punts in the year ended March 31, 1996. Turnover increased by nine percent to 141 million punts while operating profit before exceptional items was up 19 percent at 23.9 million, the company said in a statement. Bord na Mona said the 1995 peat harvest was excellent and came in at just over seven million tonnes of milled peat or about 150 percent of target.

"This was the largest milled peat harvest in the history of Bord na Mona and enabled the company to replenish peat stocks which had been run down due to a series of harvests over three years which had been affected by poor weather," Bord na Mona said.
The group said net debt increased by 0.8 percent to 167.5 million Irish pounds, due to the cost of financing the additional peat harvest and the acquisition of the coal business of CHL.
"When these are taken into account, the underlying trend in debt reduction was maintained," the company said.
Chairman Pat Dineen said the most crucial issue now facing the company was to increase profitability.
"There will be continuing pressure on overhead costs as well as continued investment to facilitate and ensure improved performance," Dineen said.
Bord na Mona said that the Irish government was planning to invest the first tranche of a proposed equity injection before the end of December 1996, subject to clearance from the European Union.
